### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/package.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/package.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 57 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8e8046b1a874eff7901ff559b29ba39cc2e0d1ec` — the merge of head `e7d50aba5d66471b4e32d885bb5aa4c39f7ef286` into base `26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8e8046b1a874eff7901ff559b29ba39cc2e0d1ec && git checkout 8e8046b1a874eff7901ff559b29ba39cc2e0d1ec
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e e7d50aba5d66471b4e32d885bb5aa4c39f7ef286 && git checkout -B drift-repro 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e && git merge --no-ff e7d50aba5d66471b4e32d885bb5aa4c39f7ef286

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `e7d50aba5d66471b4e32d885bb5aa4c39f7ef286`
Local-runs: none

Face: `declaration` (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`, amended by the seat in 6787525092; no path-derived face: `packages/cli` only, plus docs and changeset). Inputs: card #32153 with every comment, the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on this head (41 success, 17 skipped, 0 failed).

### ① Derived judgments

- `os g view NAME --object OBJECT`: FROM refused TO a views container for OBJECT whose one list view is `listViews.NAME`. A widening. **Right:** the generated container passes `defineStack`, and the dev measured `os validate` / `os lint` with zero findings on a fresh `os init` project.
- `os g action NAME --object OBJECT` in a stack with no flow: FROM refused TO a declarative `operation: 'update'` action, with `params` on the title field, else the first field, and no `list_toolbar` location, which `ActionSchema` refuses for an update. A widening. **Right.** With `--flow`, or with exactly one flow, the command behaves as before, and several flows without `--flow` are still refused. An object with no field is refused before writing (`generate.ts`: "has no field … to write"), since an update with nothing to write would itself be refused.
- `os g view` for an object that already has a views container: FROM writing a file that then fails to load TO refused before anything is written, printing the `listViews` entry to add. **Right:** no state that loaded before is refused now, so this is not a narrowing arm.
- `os g object` output style (`Field.text`, named export plus the kept default export, `details` group, barrel re-export by name) and `oclif.topics` help descriptions: output and help changes, with no accept-set change. **Right.**
- Public exports of `@objectstack/cli`: `barrelExportLine` changes its emitted line, but it is a CLI-internal helper. No published API moves.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/cli': patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. A non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3). `Check Changeset` is green on this head with the amended PR body. **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- Card items left open, as ordered:
  - the `field-no-consumers` lint alignment (`packages/lint`, spec lane; measured: a field without a group warns `inert`, with `group: 'details'` it is silent);
  - the empty-dashboard state (a `ui/**` renderer change).
  The PR is `Part of`, and the card stays open with these two as its carriers.
- Four pre-existing nightly `generate-scaffold-gates.e2e` legs (`os g app` second app; `os g permission` leaves `nav-object-ungranted` on the starter's Notes entry) reproduce at the merge base. They are not this diff's. The seat files them as their own card.
- `os init`'s object template keeps the old style: noted, no carrier. Folded into the e2e follow-up card.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-32153-generate-scaffold-style`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYm8sWjp2Pk76warN7w`

**VERDICT: PASS**
